title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
A Tesla vehicle equipped with Autopilot was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family that the vehicle's crash data had been deleted and was unavailable, but a security researcher later demonstrated that every Tesla vehicle retains this data. The crash data that was claimed to be missing showed that the vehicle had detected a hazard before the collision occurred.

This is a failure of data access and transparency in a safety-critical system. The company's statement that relevant safety data did not exist prevented the family from accessing information about what the vehicle detected and how it responded in the moments before impact. A jury ordered Tesla to pay over $240 million in the case, and a judge upheld the verdict.

It is not established from these reports what processes Tesla had for retrieving or preserving crash data, or what safeguards existed to prevent inaccurate claims about data availability to families and legal parties.
